name: Private credit stress
value: Q3 BDC requests ~11.5% of NAV vs 5% caps
summary: Non-traded BDC redemption requests still far above 5% caps; gates remain in force
state: Non-traded BDCs received Q3 redemption requests worth about 11.5% of NAV against typical 5% quarterly caps, leaving billions unmet (With Intelligence; iCapital). Blackstone's BCRED reported a 30 Sep NAV of $23.51 after paying about half of requests in Q2. No new large fund gate, forced sale or spillover to banks or insurers had been reported as of 4 Nov.
for_you: Investors in semi-liquid private credit funds may be able to withdraw only part of what they ask for each quarter. Most savers' exposure is indirect, through pensions.
rubric_hit: Large funds limiting redemptions = Watch; no multi-fund forced selling = not Alert

sources.title: With Intelligence — BDC portfolios: redemptions, NAVs and credit stress
iCapital — BDC redemptions: looking beyond the gates

why: Private credit has grown fast outside bank regulation; its losses surface late and can spill into banks, insurers and pension funds.
drivers: Defaults among leveraged mid-sized borrowers, payment-in-kind interest, fund redemption requests, bank lending to funds.

rubric.alert: Several large funds gate at once, forced asset sales, or losses spreading to banks or insurers.
rubric.watch: A large fund limits redemptions, listed BDCs trade at wide discounts to NAV, or a cluster of borrower defaults with heavy losses.
rubric.normal: No notable fund gates, defaults or markdowns beyond the routine.
